sections.h2: Where do Coweta County owners take property tax questions?
sections.html:
Newnan holds both offices owners need. The Tax Commissioner at 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, handles bills and payments, and its number is 770-254-2670. The Assessor's Office at 37 Perry Street decides values and homestead claims, and its number is 770-254-2680.

The commissioner's counter opens at 8am and closes at 4:30pm on weekdays. Two elected boards, the county commissioners and the school board, each set a millage rate, while a board named by the grand jury hears value disputes. A copy of your deed comes from the Clerk of Superior Court inside the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, and the commissioner's FAQ lists 770-254-2690 for the clerk.

  • Value or exemption: Assessor's Office.
  • Bill, payoff or lien: Tax Commissioner.
  • Deed copy: Clerk of Superior Court.

sections.h2: What is Coweta County like for someone preparing to sell?
sections.html:
Coweta County lies in the Georgia Piedmont, southwest of Atlanta, and counts as Metro Atlanta. Newnan is the seat and biggest city. The state legislature drew the county lines on June 9, 1826, after the Creek cession, and the name honors the Koweta people.

Five cities share the map: Newnan, Senoia, Grantville, Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills. Haralson, Moreland, Sharpsburg and Turin are towns. Palmetto and Chattahoochee Hills spill over into Fulton County. Local land history includes Shenandoah, a 7,400-acre planned town backed by a 1970 federal program, which was foreclosed on in 1981. Wikipedia places the eastern half of the county in the Upper Flint River basin and the western half near Lake Harding on the Chattahoochee.

Population rose from 127,317 in 2010 to 146,158 in 2020, and QuickFacts shows 160,240 for July 2025. Census five-year estimates give owned homes a typical value of $357,500, with 78.4% of households owning. Rent averages $1,488 a month, household income is $95,548, and a commute takes 29.8 minutes on average.

sections.h2: What does the Coweta County tax calendar look like?
sections.html:
The commissioner's site says bills are mailed October 1 with payment due December 1. Mailing happens at least 60 days ahead. If the date on your printed bill differs, the printed date wins.

A drop box sits in the building's drive-through, and online card payments incur a fee that the card company collects. Checks sent by mail need a postmark by the due date. A closed office on the due date pushes payment to the next open day.

For general questions about Georgia property tax outside what the county answers, the commissioner's site points owners to the state Department of Revenue's local government services division at dor.georgia.gov.

  • January 1: ownership and use on this date fix the year's tax.
  • Through April 1: returns, first-year homestead filings and special program applications.
  • April 1: mobile and manufactured home tax, with a location decal issued after payment.
  • October 1: bills go in the mail.
  • December 1: due date for land, buildings and personal property.

sections.h2: What does Coweta County charge on late bills?
sections.html:
Interest builds monthly at prime plus three percentage points. A 5% penalty first applies at day 120, adds again every 120 days, and stops at 20%. A homesteaded bill below $500 escapes the penalty.

After about a month of non-payment, the commissioner may file a FiFa lien with the superior court clerk, on the General Execution Docket. The site says the lien stays on a credit record for seven years at minimum. Delinquent notices go out only now and then, so the office tells owners to ask for the current balance before sending money.

Mobile and manufactured homes carry a different risk: a missed April 1 payment and permit brings a 10% penalty, a citation to Coweta County State Court, or possible sale of the home.

sections.h2: Who pays the Coweta County tax when a house changes hands?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is the name on the lien. A seller who receives a bill after the sale should hand it to the buyer, but the lien moves only if the commissioner gets proof of a contract or closing statement by day 90 after the due date.

So a seller whose closing prorated the tax should carry the settlement statement to Newnan Station Drive. Once the office has it, a bill that stays unpaid leads to a lien against the new owner.

Timing matters. Bills are mailed in October, so a spring or summer closing usually happens before that year's bill exists and the title company must estimate. Ask the commissioner for last year's total as a benchmark, and ask the closer how the estimate was set.

A buyer reading a Coweta County listing should also know that the bill covers the whole tax year, not just the months after the sale. When that matters in a negotiation, put the tax split in the contract in plain words so both sides and the closer work from the same page.

sections.h2: What are the three ways to appeal in Coweta County?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the assessment notice. The first move is a written appeal on the state's uniform form, filed with the Board of Assessors, and it must name the route you want. Taxability, value, uniformity and a denied exemption are all valid grounds.

Appeal routes the Coweta County Tax Commissioner describes
RouteBest suited toWhat follows
Equalization boardMost homeownersHearing, then Superior Court if needed
Hearing officerNon-homestead real property valued at $1,000,000 or moreDecision, then Superior Court if needed
ArbitrationOwners holding a current certified appraisalHearing within 30 days; the ruling is final

Under the equalization route, the assessors can revise the value and mail a new notice, which you may appeal within 30 days. An appeal they leave unchanged moves forward on its own to a hearing. For arbitration, the assessors must acknowledge the appeal within 45 days, and if they reject your appraisal they must certify the case to the Clerk of Superior Court.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special programs apply in Coweta County?
sections.html:
To claim a homestead you must have owned the house and lived in it on January 1, and the application has to arrive by April 1 of the first year. A late filing takes effect a year later. The assessors rule on every claim, a denial can be appealed, and you may not claim a homestead on any other property.

Coweta County also has local exemptions that replace the state figure whenever they are larger. The assessors will tell you what proof they want for age, income or military service. After approval the exemption renews without a new application until you move or the owner changes.

  • Deferral: for owners 62 and over with gross household income of $15,000 or less, tax waits until the ownership changes or the balance plus interest reaches 85% of fair market value.
  • Agricultural use: qualifying farmland is assessed at 30% of fair market value.
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection: covenants of 10 or 15 years.
  • Historic property and Hazardous Site Reuse: preferential assessment, each applied for in the first four months of the year it starts.

A buyer of an enrolled tract should ask the assessors whether the covenant carries over.

faqs.q: Which office in Coweta County sends my property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner, at 87 Newnan Station Drive, Suite 100, Newnan. Bills go out October 1, and you can call 770-254-2670.

faqs.q: Is December 1 the Coweta County due date for every bill?
faqs.a: For land, buildings and personal property, yes, per the commissioner's site. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, and the printed bill states the date that applies to you.

faqs.q: Can a hearing officer decide my Coweta County homestead appeal?
faqs.a: No. The county limits hearing officers to disputes over the value of non-homestead real property worth $1,000,000 or more.

faqs.q: Where do I get my deed in Coweta County?
faqs.a: From the Clerk of Superior Court at the Coweta County Justice Center, 72 Greenville Street, Newnan, GA 30263. The commissioner's FAQ gives 770-254-2690 for the clerk.

faqs.q: Do Coweta County penalties apply to every unpaid bill?
faqs.a: Not to homesteaded property with a bill under $500. Other unpaid bills take the 5% penalty after 120 days, repeating every 120 days up to a 20% cap.
